A template literal is always a non-empty string (truthy), even when both interpolations are undefined, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead code and users can see "undefined: undefined" instead of the intended fallback message. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the added code.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` onError, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (e.g. "undefined: ..."), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` will never use the fallback. This can lead to confusing error toasts like "undefined: ..." when `err.data?.code` or `err.message` isn’t set/translated, which is a real behavior defect introduced by this diff.
